caseno: Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No.226 of 2009.
lawyer:
For the Petitioner: Mr. A.K.M. Zahirul Haque, Additional Attorney General instructed by Mrs. Sufia Khatun, Advocate-on Record. 
For the Respondent: Mr. Khondaker Mahbub Hossain, Senior Advocate instructed by Mr. Syed Mahbubur Rahman, Advocate-on-Record.
parties:
The State ------ Petitioner
Versus
Md. Monwar Hossain Dipzol ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
Mr. B.K. Das J.:- This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 26.04.2009 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Misc. Case No. 422 of 2009 quashing the conviction and sentence passed against the convict-respondent Md. Monwar Hossain Dipzol by the Metropolitan Special Tribunal No. 7, Dhaka in Special Tribunal Case No. 346 of 2007 and setting the said convict Monwar Hossain Dipzol at liberty, if not wanted in any other case. 

 2. Facts of the case, in short are that One A.S.I. Md. Asaduzzaman lodged a First Information Report with Mirpur Police Station against the accused petitioner-respondent alleging inter alia that with his force along with Joint Force on 15.01.2007 at about 22:45 hours, on the basis of an information of joint force and at the order of officer in charge, he went to the house of the accused-respondent and seized several articles including one(i) .22 bore Rifle & 317 bullets of .22 bore Rifle, one(i) magazine of .22 bore, one(i) shotgun of .12 bore, one(i) licence of shotgun, one(i) DBBL Rifle with licence, one(i) Air gun, 89 cartridges with two bullets, a licence of Air gun bullets and one licence of NPB pistol in presence of the witnesses, but in the absence of the respondent. On the basis of the said allegation the police started Mirpur P.S. Case No.26(1)2007 against the respondent under section-I9A of the Arms Act. 

 5. The case was transferred to the Court to Metro.. Special No. 7, Dhaka for trial and the same is numbered as Metro. Special Tribunal Case No. 386 of 2007, who framed charges, under section-19A and 19(f) of the Arms Act against the accused respondent in his absence along with another co-accused, his wife Most. Rumana Monowar alias Rumana Akhter and after trial convicted the respondent and awarded sentence. 

 7. The convict-respondent then filed Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 422 of 2009 in the High Court Division praying for bail under section 56IA of the Code of Criminal Procedure upon challenging the judgment and order of his conviction and sentence dated 26.07.2007 passed by the Metro. Special Tribunal No.7, Dhaka in Metro. Special Tribunal Case No. 346 of 2007 arising out of Mirpur Police Station Case No. 26(1)2007 convicting him under sections 19A and 19(f) of the Arms Act and sentenced him to suffer rigorous imprisonment 10 years and for 7 years respectively to run concurrently. 

 8. A Division Bench of the High Court Division upon hearing the parties made the rule absolute and conviction and sentence passed against the respondent Md. Monowar Hossain Dipjol and sentencing him u/s 19A and 19(f) of the Arms Act for a period of 10 years and 7 years respectively by the Metropolitan Special Tribunal No. 7, Dhaka in Special Tribunal Case No. 346 of 2007 were quashed. 

 9. The convict-respondent Monowar Hossain Dipjol was directed to be set at liberty at once, if not wanted in any other case. 

 11. Mr. A.K.M. Zahirul Haque, the learned Additional Attorney General appears on behalf of the petitioner in both the cases while Mr. Khondaker Mahbub Hossain, the learned Senior Advocate appears on behalf of the respondents in both cases. 

 12. We have heard the submissions of the learned Advocate for both the parties and perused the impugned order including all other papers available on record. The learned Additional Attorney. General submits that the High Court Division while making the rule absolute have not appreciated correctly that the proceeding against the accused involves information from reliable source and the informant being A.S.I. with his force along with joint force recovered huge arms and ammunitions from the residence of the convict respondent and after conclusion of the trial the trial court found the accused guilty of the offence under sections 19A and 19(f) of the Arms Act and the High Court Division erroneously quashed the conviction and sentence of the respondents. The learned Additional Attorney General next submits that the impugned order clearly shows non-application of judicial mind by the learned Judges of the High Court Division as the matter involves the question of facts as to the genuineness of the licences of the huge arms and ammunitions which have to be proved by evidence. The learned Additional Attorney General further submits that the learned Judges of the High Court Division failed to consider that the convict respondent was a fugitive at the trial having knowledge about of the criminal cases against hint, and he did not care to face the trial and kept himself out of justice and thereby disentitled him from any relief by way of quashmant the conviction and sentence under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 14. It appears that the prosecution examined as many as 10 witnesses out of charge sheet continuous in Metro Special Tribunal Case No.346 of 2007. The accused respondent could not be examined under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure as he was tried in absentia the High Court Division noticed "The FIR story of both the cases manifest that a number of Arms along with Ammunitions have been seized from the residential house of the petitioner. During the trial before the Metropolitan Special Tribunal No.7, Dhaka as many as 25 witnesses were examined in both the case and all most all of them have allegedly proved the recovery of the Arms from the residential house of the petitioner. All those witnesses were cross-examined on behalf of the co-accused, the wife of the petitioner one Rumana Monwar Hossain @ Rumana Akter. From the trend of cross-examination, it appears that the accused persons suggestion revelved the case of the petitioner that on the previous day a joint task force raided the house of the petitioner on 15.01.2007 and taken way all license of the arms and seized lawful ammunition from the house of the petitioner and later on 08.03.2007 no ammunitions were recovered from the house of the petitioner but in order to implicate the petitioner falsely the Mirpur Police Station Case No. 34(3) of 2007 was lodged." The learned Judges of the High Court Division considered relevant provisions of the Arms Act noticed "In view the aforesaid provision, it appears that the defence case of existence of license in respect of the seized Arms and Ammunitions is a vital aspect to be considered in order to come to a safe finding that the accused person committed the offence under section 19 which includes sub section (0 and also the related supplementary section 19A of the Arms Act 1878. Unless such a determination is made by the trial court, this court holds that any contravention of such vital principle of trial shall definitely, vitiate the trial." The learned Judges further noticed "The petitioner inscribed the format of the license in the body of the substantive petition wherefrom it appears that license 'No. 39/25/99 was issued for NPB Pistol (.32 bore) being No.F32733E along with the ammunitions to be purchased by the license holder within one year to the extent of hundred piece. This license has been renewed on 22.07.2005 for four years from 2005 to 2008. 

 The petitioner further inscribed the license No. 39/18/99 issued for 12 bore short gun bearing No. MV16855G along with ammunition unlimited to be purchased by the license holder having me license renewed on 25.07.2005 up to the year 2008. These two licenses was issued in the name Anowar Hossain, a brother of the petitioner." The learned Judges of the High Court Division then considered the other matter and noticed "In Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 422 of 2007 the petitioner has inscribed further draft copies of the license as has been issued by the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka, in respect of the seized Arms wherefrom it appears that the draft copy of license No. 39/13/2005 has been issued for point .22 bore rifle No. 146/117 along with the authority to purchase ammunitions hundred pieces in one year. This license is valid up 31.12.2008. 

 The draft format of license No. 39/60/92 has been issued for one .12 bore shot gun (SBBL) being No.L-2015056 having the license renewed up to 2009." The learned Judges on consideration of the materials placed on record found that the teamed Tribunal Judge upon calculating the quantity of the ammunition came to the finding that the petitioner was holding excess quantity of ammunitions then the license allowed, but this court finds that while the learned Tribunal Judge was calculating the quantity of the Arms only relied on the Arms owned by the petitioner and did not, take into consideration the Arms that were owned by his brother and kept in custody of the petitioner along with the license of the Arms. The learned Judges of the High Court Division found that the learned Tribunal Judge committed error as to holding of  excess ammunition by the convict petitioner which being erroneous requires interference by this court. The learned Judges further noticed that if a criminal case is based upon preposterous fact then the same may be a ground for interference by the High Court Division into a decision given by the Sub-ordinate Court, as it renders 'the decision a nullity. The learned Judges then noticed "More so when the accused persons are repeatedly claiming that production of Criminal records of the licenses from the office of Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka shall prove that they have not committed any offence under the Arms Act, a non-consideration of such aspect has vital effect upon the entire which cannot be ignored by the Division Bench. Accordingly, by the impugned judgment and order dated 26.04.2009 the Division Bench made the rule absolute and "The conviction and sentence passed against the conviction-petitioner Md. Monwar Hossain Dipjal by the Metropolitan Special Tribunal No. 7, Dhaka in Special Tribunal Case No. 320 of 2007 and 346 of 2007 are hereby quashed." The convict appellant Monowar Hossain Dipjol be set at liberty at once, if not wanted in any other case." In view of the aforesaid finding of the High Court Division we do not find any substance in any of the submission of the learned Additional Attorney General on behalf of the petitioner.
